Easy to mix up

Most kanji mistakes come from two places: kanji that look alike, and readings that change from word to word. Skim both tables before any quiz.

Look-alike kanji

Look-alikesHow to tell them apart
日 月 目 白日 (sun, day) is a short box with one bar in the middle. 月 (moon, month) is taller and narrower, with two bars and a hook that curves to the left. 目 (eye) is a straight-sided box with two bars. 白 (white) is 日 with a small slash on top.
白 百百 (hundred) is 白 with a bar added on top.
木 本 休木 (tree) with a bar near the bottom becomes 本 (origin, book). 休, as in 休日 (holiday), is a person 人 leaning on a tree 木.
木 水 火木 has a straight vertical stroke. 水 has a hooked vertical stroke with a splash on each side. 火 looks like a flame with a spark on each side.
人 八人 (person) has its two legs joined at the top. 八 (eight) is two separate strokes that never touch.
七 十七 (seven) is like a 十 whose vertical stroke bends to the right at the bottom. 十 (ten) is a plain cross.
十 千 土 士十 is a plain cross. 千 (thousand) is a 十 with a slanted hat on top. 土 (earth) has two bars, and the lower one is longer. 士 is the opposite, with the upper bar longer. It showed up as a wrong choice in the workbook.
子 字 学 好子 (child) is the base. 字 is 子 under a roof. 学 is 子 under a small crown and a roof. 好 is 女 next to 子. All three of these were wrong choices for こども in the workbook.
母 毎 女母 (mother) is 女 with two dots inside. 毎 (every, as in 毎月) is the same shape with a small hat on top.
男 田 力男 (man) is 田 (rice field) sitting on top of 力 (power).
友 反 刀In 友 (friend), the slanting stroke at the start cuts through the top bar. In 反, that stroke hangs from the end of the bar instead. 刀 (sword) is a different, simpler shape. 反 and 刀 were both wrong choices in the workbook.
四 西 酒 兄四 (four) is a box with two short legs inside. 西 (west) is a lid over a box. 酒 (sake) has the water mark on its left side. 兄 (older brother) is a mouth 口 on top of a person. Only 四 belongs to this workbook.

Reading traps

KanjiWatch out forWhat to remember
一日ついたち or いちにちついたち is the 1st of the month. いちにち is one whole day.
二十日はつか or はたちはつか is the 20th day. はたち is age 20, not a date.
日Lots of readingsひ (sun, day), び (weekday names), にち (にちようび, 十一にち), か (the ending of ふつか, みっか and the rest up to とおか), じつ (きゅうじつ), に (にほん).
日 火Both are read ひ日 is sun or day, 火 is fire. In the weekdays, 日よう日 is にちようび and 火よう日 is かようび.
四し, よん, よよん is the plain number. よ appears in よにん and よっつ. し appears in しがつ.
七しち or ななしち in しちがつ and しちじ. なな in ななつ and ななひゃく. 七日 is なのか.
九く or きゅうく in くがつ and くじ. きゅう in きゅうじゅうきゅう and きゅうふん. 九日 is ここのか and 九つ is ここのつ.
十じゅう, じゅっ, とおじゅう is the plain number. じゅっ comes before さい and ぷん. とお is ten pieces, and 十日 is とおか.
月がつ, かげつ, つき, げつがつ for month names (しがつ). かげつ for how many months (さんかげつ). つき on its own (まいつき). げつ in げつようび and こんげつ.
人ひと, り, にん, じんひとり and ふたり are the only two with り. From three on it is にん, except よにん (not よんにん). People of a nation use じん, like にほんじん.
何人なんにん or なにじんなんにん asks how many people. なにじん asks what nationality. Same kanji, different question.
何なに or なんなに on its own or before か (なにか). なん before です or a counter like 本 or 人 (なんですか, なんぼん).
日本 二本Both can be にほん日本 is Japan (にほん or にっぽん). 二本 is two long objects. The kanji tells you which one.
本ほん, ぽん, ぼんぽん after 1, 6, 8, 10 and 100. ぼん after 3 and 何. ほん after 2, 4, 5, 7 and 9.
千 百Sounds changeさんぜん, はっせん, さんびゃく, ろっぴゃく, はっぴゃく. See the sound-change table above.
父 母ちち, はは or おとうさん, おかあさんちち and はは are for your own parents when talking to other people. おとうさん and おかあさん are for someone else's parents, and for talking to your own parents.
子こ or しこ in こども and おとこのこ. し in だんし and じょし.
金きん or かねきん in きんようび and gold. かね in おかね (money).
男 女Small んおとこ has no ん. おんな has one. Same in おとこのこ and おんなのこ.

docs.html:
Answers for every exercise in the Kanji Workbook N5, Lessons 1 to 3 (kanji 1 to 30, workbook pages 9 to 21). That is 120 items: 10 each in れんしゅう I, れんしゅう II, テスト I and テスト II, for each of the three lessons. The workbook's own answer key is at the back of the full book and was not in the pages you shared, so these answers were worked out from the lessons and the word lists. Use this file together with the Kanji 1 Reviewer.

How the exercises work

  • れんしゅう I: write the hiragana reading of the underlined kanji.
  • れんしゅう II: the word is given in hiragana. Write it in kanji and give the English meaning. The workbook's example is おおきい, 大きい, big.
  • テスト I: pick the right hiragana reading from four choices.
  • テスト II: pick the right kanji from four choices.

In the tests, the answer is the number of the correct choice, with the choice itself in brackets.

items.b: Sound rules that trip people up
items.h: 1. Small tsu (っ ッ) doubles the next consonant. You hold a tiny pause before it. がっこう is gak-kou (school), きっぷ is kip-pu (ticket) and きって is kit-te (postal stamp). In katakana, ベッド is bed-do (bed) and カップ is kap-pu (cup).

cells: ごろ is around a point in time. ぐらい is about how long.

items.b: Easy to mix up
cells: から, まで or で

items.b: Easy to mix up
cells: ~じ is a clock time and ~じかん is a length of time. なんじに asks when, なんじかん asks how long.

items.x: じ or じかん | ~じ is a clock time and ~じかん is a length of time. なんじに asks when, なんじかん asks how long. | じゅうじはんに ねます (at 10:30) and じゅうじかん ねます (for 10 hours)

items.b: Easy to mix up
cells: An い-adjective ends in く before a verb, and a な-adjective takes に. Before a noun, a な-adjective takes な.

cells: ません or ませんでした

items.b: Easy to mix up › Markers that look alike
cells: で goes with an action verb. に goes with います or あります.
かいしゃで はたらきます (I work at the company) vs かいしゃに います (I am at the company)

items.b: Easy to mix up › Markers that look alike
cells: Does the other person do the action too? If they join you, use と. If they only receive it, use に.

items.b: Easy to mix up › Markers that look alike

items.b: Kanji list › How readings work
items.h: Most kanji have two kinds of reading. The workbook calls them the Japanese reading (kun'yomi) and the Chinese reading (on'yomi).

items.b: Kanji list › How readings work
items.h: The Japanese reading is meaning-based. It is the original Japanese word, and you usually see it when the kanji stands alone or has kana after it, as in 一つ (ひとつ).
items.x: The Japanese reading is meaning-based. It is the original Japanese word, and you usually see it when the kanji stands alone or has kana after it, as in 一つ (ひとつ).

items.b: Kanji list › How readings work
items.h: The Chinese reading is sound-based. You usually see it inside compound words, as in 一月 (いちがつ).

items.b: Easy to mix up › Look-alike kanji
cells: 日 月 目 白

日 (sun, day) is a short box with one bar in the middle. 月 (moon, month) is taller and narrower, with two bars and a hook that curves to the left. 目 (eye) is a straight-sided box with two bars. 白 (white) is 日 with a small slash on top.
